mostWorthwhile.text: Building living supporting tissue was most worthwhile: the planned pictures connect collagen secretion and assembly to a tissue containing both cells and extracellular matrix.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial differentiation conditions felt less engaging than the later constructions: the timed lineage was supplied rather than explored, and terms such as mesoderm and mesenchymal progenitors were not explained.

surprise.text: The muscle branch stopped at separate, single-nucleus myoblasts rather than producing mature fibres; the contrast with the fibroblasts' exported collagen clarified their different work.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although combining fibroblasts with the matrix they had just produced felt somewhat repetitive; it did clarify that tissue includes both.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in seeing how the myoblasts develop into mature muscle, since this chapter deliberately leaves that process unfinished.
